title: Booze Buddy
summary: A UX-focused mobile app prototype promoting safer drinking habits for university students navigating social drinking culture.
overview: The project was created to explore how design can address social drinking in student life. Through this project, I aimed to apply UX principles to promote harm reduction and social connection, focusing on user-centered design practices.
problem: How might we support young adults in developing healthier drinking habits while still feeling socially confident?
objective: To promote safe and mindful drinking by reducing risks through accessible tools that enable real-time decision-making.
solution: Booze Buddy meets students where they are — real-time drink tracking, a help center, and safer choices without sacrificing social confidence.

title: King's Pastry
summary: AI-assisted marketing design — print, web mockups, and analytics for a local bakery.
videoDesc: High-fidelity landing pages with market data callouts, product imagery, and clear CTAs.
overview: Marketing design for a seasonal bakery brand — product launches across print and web, with AI tools supporting front-end setup and analytics.
problem: How might we grow brand presence across print and digital without a full in-house team?
objective: Ship cohesive campaign assets and measure engagement using AI-assisted workflows.
solution: Sell sheets, landing pages, and event collateral — plus faster front-end and analytics setup.

challenges.title: AI-Assisted Workflow
challenges.body: Used AI to generate the Google Analytics 4 install snippet for Webflow, then monitored traffic, geography, and engagement to inform marketing decisions.

challenges.title: Print & Campaign Design
challenges.body: Posters and sell sheets for the Ube Jelly Roll and Pandan Mini Mousse Cake launches.

images.label: Street poster — ube jelly roll & pandan mousse

challenges.title: Marketing Collateral
challenges.body: Menu cards and pull-up banners for the Mini Bundt Cakes twin-pack campaign.

title: Neko Beat
summary: A rhythm game exploring Parkinson's through controlled friction — designed in Figma and built with p5.js using Cursor.
videoDesc: Screen recording of Neko Beat in play — timing notes, combos, and misses.
overview: Built for a design brief on representing a human condition through interaction. I led visual and interaction design, then co-developed the game in p5.js with Cursor — using AI to implement HUD, controls, and gameplay systems from design decisions.
problem: Parkinson's is widely recognized but rarely understood experientially — most representations focus on symptoms, not the lived difficulty of intentional movement and timing.
objective: Design a rhythm game that introduces controlled friction in timing and coordination, while staying engaging and playable.
solution: Notes travel down lanes toward a hit bar. Players start with F and J, then unlock more keys in later levels. Mistimed presses create friction that echoes disrupted motor control — not as a clinical simulation, but as a felt timing challenge.

challenges.title: Timing friction
challenges.body: A mistimed press breaks the combo and flashes Miss — immediate feedback so players feel the cost of imperfect timing without leaving the game fantasy.

challenges.title: AI-assisted development
challenges.body: Used Cursor to turn design ideas into working code — multi-file edits for score/combo HUD, pause overlay, mute controls, and keyboard instruction clarity. I directed the gameplay intent; AI accelerated implementation across HTML, CSS, and sketch.js.

challenges.title: Controls & coordination
challenges.body: Players start with F and J (left/right hand), then later levels add more keys. Split-hand timing forces bilateral coordination under pressure.

challenges.title: Visual language
challenges.body: Synthwave neon and kawaii characters keep the tone approachable, so the friction feels like a game challenge rather than a clinical demo.

title: Sweet Soaperie
summary: Website redesign for a Canadian handmade bath brand — clearer shopping flows, stronger hierarchy, and a sweeter brand feel.
overview: A redesign of The Sweet Soaperie — a handmade bath product brand based in Miramichi, NB. The goal was a more user-friendly, visually cohesive digital experience that matches the brand’s sweet, joyful personality.
problem: How might we redesign The Sweet Soaperie’s website to better showcase products, improve usability, and reflect their joyful brand personality?
objective: Improve visual hierarchy and layout, simplify navigation, and enhance product pages with clearer content and richer imagery.
solution: A cleaner shopping experience with clearer hierarchy, accessible pastel contrast, multi-image product storytelling, and a cohesive footer — balancing playful brand expression with usability for a small-business e-commerce site.

challenges.title: Homepage & shop
challenges.body: Restructured the homepage around best sellers and a clearer Shop Now path, with a product grid that makes browsing feel inviting instead of cluttered.

challenges.title: Product storytelling
challenges.body: Expanded Explore moments like “Bath bombs in action” with richer imagery, ingredients context, and related products — fixing thin pages that previously relied on a single vague image.

challenges.title: Contact & find a store
challenges.body: Simplified the contact journey with a clear form and store-finder section so customers can reach the brand without hunting through cluttered nav.

challenges.title: Brand presence
challenges.body: Kept soft pastel identity while improving contrast and packaging-adjacent photography so the digital experience feels as clean as the products.

title: Sprout
summary: A 12-hour UX design jam app helping young Canadian parents budget with goals and community support.
overview: Sprout is a mobile budgeting app concept from the 2024 uXperience Design Jam — designed in a 12-hour sprint to help young Canadian parents feel more confident with financial tools during a major life transition. Our team placed third.
problem: How might we help young Canadians discover and use financial tools and education tailored to their needs — especially new parents overwhelmed by money stress?
objective: Make financial planning less intimidating through clear, goal-based budgeting and a supportive parent community.
solution: A calm, approachable interface with goal tracking, simple contributions, and a community space — soft greens, clear hierarchy, and parent-focused flows that feel supportive instead of judgmental.

challenges.title: Key screens
challenges.body: Splash, login, add-to-goal, home, community, and profile — designed in a 12-hour sprint with a calm sage palette and clear hierarchy.

title: UX Explorations
summary: Self-directed design challenges — invite flows, onboarding, and multi-step mobile UI craft.
overview: A living space for UI craft. Short design challenges where I practice clarity, feedback, and visual polish on everyday product patterns — starting with team invites and join flows.
problem: How might we make inviting teammates and joining a product feel effortless instead of tedious?
objective: Design high-fidelity mobile flows that feel light, clear, and rewarding — with minimal input and obvious next steps.
solution: Soft gradients, pill controls, and step-by-step progress keep attention on one action at a time — whether sending invites or finishing a short onboarding.

challenges.title: Inviting teammates
challenges.body: Add multiple people by email or link, set roles inline, and send invites with clear feedback — so collaboration setup feels quick instead of admin-heavy.

challenges.title: Joining & accepting
challenges.body: A short sign-up path with progress cues and a small delight moment — unlocking a profile badge — so onboarding stays focused and rewarding.
